answer: Voting weight can come only from repeated escrowed trades with distinct counterparties who confirm delivery; new identities begin with none, and duplicate confirmations from one party do not count. The ledger links accounts funded by the same source, so splitting one wallet into cedar, trellis, and jetty identities adds no influence. To evade this, an attacker needs separate funds, many real trades, and deposits at risk of being slashed for fraud.
